chapter: Chicago: Henderson, Tatum and Roy Eldridge, then New York and the army
title: Jam sessions at the Three Deuces: Waller, Basie's band, Lester Young
summary: Touring bands came to the club, Fats Waller brought his band to jam, and Basie's band, on their first trip out of Kansas City, jammed all night with Lester Young and Ben Webster.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: At this time, when I was working at the Three Deuces with Roy, all -- as I said, all the musicians came in. That's -- oh, just Red Norville, Mildred Bailey, their band of just all the great bands. So it was kind of a showcase, and we had a very good band, and we were broadcasting from there. Basie had a little six piece band or seven piece band that was broadcasting from Kansas City at the time, and they came on just before, so we would sit in the car and hear them, and then when they'd go off we'd rush in and we'd start broadcasting. And Fats Waller would bring his whole band in and jam with us, this is the truth. They had a big band, they had a 16 piece band and he'd have them lined all around the tables. He would bring his whole band in and jam, on the bandstand. I said no black musicians came in there. That's not true. Shuberry would come in. On the stands some nights would be Shuberry, Ben Webster, Lester, they all at the same time. Don Byas. This is in Chicago now, this is before New York.
This was with -- Lester was with Basie.

They left Kansas City and they came to the Grand Terrace. This was their first trip out of Kansas City. This was a trip before -- this was the engagement, rather, before they went to New York. They were on their way to New York then. They had a guitar player with them then, incidentally, by the name of -- oh, gosh, I can't remember his name. He played violin also. But it wasn't Freddy Green. I think his name was Williamson, something else. I'll think of it. But a very good guitarist. And played violin, fiddle like Stuff. That style.

But any way, they would come down and Count Basie would come to the club in a raincoat, and it was 10 below zero. They were that poor. But any way, tremendous -- musically it was just something else. Chy Choo, Ben, you know, Prez, it was -- they were all different. But they ---
Yeah, just all night long we just jammed. It was just a most rewarding experience, and good, you know.
